evidence_items.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism

evidence_items.explanation: The March–April survey found limited routine use but also practical uses and generally positive assessments among users. These findings qualify an absolute denial of utility without establishing equivalence to either historical boom.
Pew measured smartphone ownership among American adults. This supplies a historical reference, but ownership in 2011 cannot be treated as the same measure as routine AI use in 2024.

evidence_items.explanation: The paper places this GPT-4 estimate five years after its 2017 comparison. It documents expensive historical training, but does not measure industry-wide development and operating expenses during the target period.

This contemporary account describes projected full-year OpenAI expenses, not realized expenses for the target period. It is secondary reporting because the underlying article could not be read and no equivalent primary financial disclosure was retrieved.

unresolved_gaps: No matched comparison of sustained practical benefits across generative AI, early cloud services and smartphones was established.
The available cost evidence covers earlier training or projected annual spending, rather than both realized development and operating expenses in the target period.
The wording supplies no benchmark for deciding when useful adoption reaches the claimed historical scale.
